cn: 只有真正在那个国家生活，才谈得上了解它的文化。
en: You come to understand a culture only once you have lived in that country.
r: 「て形＋こそ」是“只有做到了才……”。「したこそ」接续不成立。
re: て-form + こそ means “only once you have…”. したこそ is not a valid connection.

cn: 程度虽有差别，但做了坏事这一点大家都一样。
en: The degree may differ, but everyone did something wrong just the same.
r: 「こそあれ」先承认有差别，再强调后面的共同点。
re: こそあれ grants a difference, then stresses what is still the same.

cn: 他字是难看，可文章写得好。
en: His handwriting is poor, but he writes well.
r: 「こそ…が」只承认这一点（字难看），后半转折。
re: こそ…が concedes just this one point, then contrasts.

cn: 这里虽然不方便，可绿很多，是个好地方。
en: It is inconvenient, but there is lots of greenery and it is a nice place.
r: な形容词要用「词干＋でこそあれ」。「不便なこそ」接不上。
re: A na-adjective takes でこそあれ. 不便なこそ does not connect.

cn: 文章被人理解了才有意义。
en: A piece of writing means something only once it is understood.
r: 「されてこそ」才是「される」的て形＋こそ。「こそされて」把こそ放错了位置。
re: されてこそ is the て-form of される plus こそ. こそされて misplaces こそ.

cn: 你做的事只会受到称赞，绝不会被责备。
en: What you did can only be praised, never blamed.
r: 排成「ほめられこそすれ、非難されるものではない」：只会受赞，绝不会被批评。
re: The order is ほめられこそすれ…ものではない: only praise, never blame.

cn: 这两件产品名字虽然不同，内容并没有太大差别。
en: These two products have different names, but the contents are not very different.
r: 「名前こそ違うが」只承认名字不同，后面说实质一样。
re: 名前こそ違うが concedes only the name.

cn: 我大概去不了，请当作我不在，把事情往下谈。
en: I probably cannot go, so please carry on as if I were not there.
r: 「ないものとして」是“姑且当作没有／不在”来处理。
re: ないものとして means treat it as if it were not the case.

cn: 与其看着所爱的人因病受苦，不如自己生病。
en: I would rather fall ill myself than watch someone I love suffer.
r: 「くらいなら、…ほうがいい」是“与其……不如……”。
re: くらいなら…ほうがいい means “better to… than to…”.

cn: 与其被调动到那种乡下，不如辞职。
en: I would rather quit than be transferred to a place that rural.
r: 同样是「くらいなら、…ほうがいい」：宁可辞职也不接受那种调动。
re: Same pattern: quitting is preferable to that transfer.

cn: 我买得起的房子，也就是这种程度了。
en: A house I can afford is about this level.
r: 「これぐらいのものだ」把程度往低了说：不过如此。
re: これぐらいのものだ plays the level down: nothing more than this.

cn: 合同到期时，应当另行签订新合同。
en: When a contract expires, a new one shall be concluded.
r: 「ものとする」是规定、视为“应当如此”。「ものになる」是“成为那样”，不用于规章。
re: ものとする states a rule. ものになる does not.

cn: 昨天课上讲的内容就当作大家懂了，接着往下讲。
en: We will proceed on the assumption that you understood yesterday’s lesson.
r: 「わかったものとして」把“已经懂了”当作前提继续。
re: わかったものとして takes “you understood” as the premise and moves on.

cn: 与其被人逼着做那种事，还不如不参加。
en: I would rather not take part than be made to do something like that.
r: 「させられるくらいなら、…ほうがましだ」：与其被迫做，不参加还好一点。
re: くらいなら…ほうがましだ: not joining is the lesser evil.

cn: 人如果不互相帮助，就活不下去。
en: People cannot live without helping one another.
r: 「ことなしに」是“如果不……就……”，后半多接否定。
re: ことなしに means “without doing…”, usually followed by a negative.

cn: 以她那么开朗的性子，到哪儿都能很快交到朋友吧。
en: Someone as cheerful as her will make friends quickly anywhere.
r: 「彼女のことだから」是凭对她的了解所作的判断。
re: のことだから judges from what you know of that person.

cn: 他把哥哥写的报告当作自己写的交了上去。
en: He submitted the report his brother wrote as if he had written it.
r: 「ことにして」是“权且当成／假装成”某一事实。
re: ことにして means to treat or pretend that something is the case.

cn: 为了不迷路，我事先用地图确认了地点。
en: So as not to get lost, I checked the place on a map beforehand.
r: 「ことのないように」表示“为了不要发生……”。
re: ことのないように means “so that … will not happen”.

cn: 她至今一直没吃过苦就活过来了。
en: She has lived until now without ever having a hard time.
r: 「したことなしに」是“不曾……就……”。「する」是现在形，和“至今”的经历不合。
re: したことなしに fits a past experience. The plain する does not.

cn: 他出了名地小气，就算一百日元大概也不会借给你。
en: He is famously stingy, so he probably would not lend you even 100 yen.
r: 「彼のことだから」凭对他的了解下判断：小气到一百日元也不借。
re: のことだから bases the guess on what everyone knows about him.

cn: 不证明那两者的关联，就很难解决。
en: It is hard to solve this without proving how the two are related.
r: 「ことなしに」：缺少“证明”这一步，解决就困难。
re: ことなしに: without that proof, a solution is difficult.

cn: 大家都在等新火箭完成。
en: The completion of the new rocket is eagerly awaited.
r: 「待たれる」是自发的被动：人们自然地盼着。
re: 待たれる is the spontaneous passive: people naturally look forward to it.

cn: 他缺少作为社会人应有的知识。
en: He lacks the knowledge expected of a working adult.
r: 「必要とされている」是“被（社会）认为有必要”。
re: 必要とされている is what is regarded as necessary.

cn: 要让我们这一代人来说，他的行为并不寻常。
en: If you ask people of our generation, his behavior is not normal.
r: 「に言わせれば」是“若由某人来说／依某人的看法”。
re: に言わせれば introduces whose view is being given.

cn: 那是一部让人认真思考死亡的电影。
en: It was a film that made you think seriously about death.
r: 「考えさせられる」是使役被动：不由得被逼着去想。
re: 考えさせられる is causative-passive: you are made to think.

cn: 这种新药有效，但据说副作用很强。
en: This new drug works, but it is said to have strong side effects.
r: 「とされている」是“一般认为、被看作”。「ことにされている」是“被规定成”，这里是传闻评价，不是规章。
re: とされている means “is considered”. ことにされている would mean it is officially set that way.

cn: 听说年轻人移居海外的人在增加，那个国家的将来令人担忧。
en: Young people moving abroad are said to be increasing, and that country’s future is a worry.
r: 「案じられている」是“被人担忧着”，和「増加している」一起说明现状。
re: 案じられている is the spontaneous passive: the future is worried about.

cn: 从他的话里能感到没什么干劲，可要让我说，那不过是撒娇。
en: His words made him sound unmotivated, but if you ask me that is just being spoiled.
r: 「私に言わせれば」引出说话人自己的判断，和前面的感觉相对。
re: 私に言わせれば marks the speaker’s own judgment against the earlier impression.

cn: 如果要换车的话，下一辆我想要德国车。
en: If I were to replace my car, I would want a German one next.
r: 「とすれば」是“假如如此的话”。
re: とすれば sets up a hypothetical.

cn: 她看来吃过苦，显得比实际年龄老。
en: She seems to have had a hard life; she looks older than she is.
r: 「とみえて」是根据外观所作的推测：看来是吃过苦。
re: とみえて is an inference from how she looks.

cn: 从她平时的成绩来看，人们认为她肯定能考上。
en: Judging from her usual grades, she is seen as certain to pass.
r: 「とみられている」是“被大家看作”。
re: とみられている means the public regards it that way.

cn: 他一看对方是地方出身的女性，马上就搭话。
en: As soon as he sees that a woman is from the countryside, he speaks to her.
r: 「だとみると」是“一看出是……就”。
re: だとみると means “the moment he takes someone for…”.

cn: 假如他是犯人，犯罪动机又是什么呢。
en: If he is the culprit, what was the motive?
r: 「だとすると」是假设“如果是这样”。「だとみえて」是推测外观，不能用来设这个假设。
re: だとすると is the hypothesis. だとみえて would only guess from appearances.

cn: 景气被认为正在恢复，但我觉得实际有感受的人很少。
en: The economy is seen as recovering, but I think few people actually feel it.
r: 「とみられている」表示外界的看法，和后半“实际感受”相对。
re: とみられている is the outside view, set against what people actually feel.

cn: 即使流感看起来好了，病毒有时还在，所以请再继续吃一阵药。
en: Even if the flu seems gone, the virus can remain, so keep taking the medicine for a while.
r: 「治ったとみえても」是“即便看上去像是好了”。
re: とみえても: even when it looks as if it has cleared.

cn: 无论怎么跑，绝对也来不及了吧。
en: No matter how fast you run, you will never make it.
r: 「たところで」接在过去形后，表示“即便做了也（没用）”。
re: たところで means “even if you did…”, with a useless result.

cn: 百忙之中还请各位聚集，非常感谢。
en: Thank you for gathering when you are so busy.
r: 「お忙しいところを」是“在您正忙的时候还……”，后面常接感谢或请求。
re: ところを marks an inconvenient moment, often before thanks.

cn: “你一个月大概买多少张CD？”“差不多五张吧。”
en: “About how many CDs do you buy a month?” “Around five.”
r: 「というところだ」表示大致的数量或程度。
re: というところだ gives a rough figure.

cn: 他的债，就算每天不停地干活，也不是还得起的数目。
en: His debt is not an amount he could repay even by working every day without a break.
r: 「働いたところで」同样是“即便做了也……”。
re: たところで again: even that effort would not be enough.

cn: 想让那么固执的父亲戒烟，也是白费。
en: Trying to make that stubborn father quit smoking is pointless.
r: 「ようとしたって」是「ようとしても」的口语：即便打算让他戒也没用。「にしたって」接的不是这个意志形。
re: ようとしたって is the spoken ようとしても. にしたって does not follow the volitional.

cn: 无论多么后悔做过的事，也改变不了过去。
en: However much you regret what you did, you cannot change the past.
r: 「たところで」强调后悔也于事无补。
re: たところで: regret does not change the past.

cn: 厕所自不必说，连厨房都有，这辆车简直就是会跑的家。
en: It even has a kitchen, not just a toilet — this car is practically a house that drives.
r: 「といったところだ」这里用来给事物定位：差不多就是“会跑的家”。
re: といったところだ labels what it amounts to.

cn: 他这个人，一回到家就坐到电脑前。
en: That guy sits down at the computer the moment he gets home.
r: 「帰るなり」是“一……马上就”。
re: なり means “the moment…, immediately”.

cn: 我是外行，但试着用自己的方式解释了这首诗。
en: I am an amateur, but I tried to interpret the poem in my own way.
r: 「なりに」是“以与之相称的方式、就自己的水平”。
re: なりに means in a way that fits that person or level.

cn: 你脸色不好。坐下也好、躺下也好，请放松。
en: You look pale. Sit or lie down — make yourself comfortable.
r: 「なり…なり」列举“或者……或者……都行”。
re: なり…なり lists acceptable alternatives.

cn: 一开窗，就飞进来一只怪虫子。
en: The moment I opened the window, a strange insect came in.
r: 「たとたん」是“刚一……就（发生了意外的事）”。
re: たとたん is “the instant…”, often something unexpected.

cn: 就算错过末班电车，也要打车或者走着，一定要回家。
en: Even if you miss the last train, take a taxi or walk, but get home.
r: 「乗るなり歩くなり」是“打车也好走路也好”。
re: なり…なり: taxi or walking, either is fine.

cn: 要想拿高分，就得做与之相称的准备。
en: If you aim for a high score, you need preparation to match.
r: 「それなりの」是“与那个目标相称的”。
re: それなりの means preparation fitting that aim.

cn: 杂务也好别的也好，如果需要请尽管吩咐。
en: Errands or whatever else — just say if you need something.
r: 「なりなんなり」是“……也好什么也好”的随意列举。
re: なりなんなり is a casual “or whatever else”.

cn: 他不管是早上还是半夜，都毫无顾忌地打电话来。
en: He calls without caring whether it is morning or the middle of the night.
r: 「だろうが…だろうが」是“无论是……还是……”。
re: だろうが…だろうが means “whether… or…”.

cn: 这房间里无论怎么吵，外面都听不见。
en: No matter how much noise you make in this room, nothing is heard outside.
r: 「ようとも」是“即使……也”。
re: ようとも means “even if…”.

cn: 哪怕下雨或下雪，明天的比赛也照计划进行。
en: Whether it rains or snows, tomorrow’s match will go ahead as planned.
r: 「であろうと…であろうと」是书面的“无论……还是……”。
re: であろうと…であろうと is the written “whether… or…”.

cn: 无论是哪所大学，升学去向定下来就松了口气。
en: Whichever university it is, I was relieved once the destination was set.
r: 「であれ」是“无论是……”。
re: であれ means “whatever / whichever”.

cn: 你想做什么是你的自由，但不能给别人添麻烦。
en: You are free to do what you like, but you may not trouble others.
r: 「しようと」是“即使想做……也”，后半给出限制。
re: しようと grants the freedom, then the second clause limits it.

cn: 那对夫妻变成什么样我不管，但我觉得孩子可怜。
en: I do not care what happens to that couple, but I feel sorry for the child.
r: 「どうなろうが」是“无论变成什么样（都与我无关）”。
re: どうなろうが dismisses whatever becomes of them.

cn: 不管是不是故意，伤到人这一点是不会变的。
en: Whether or not it was intentional, the fact that someone was hurt does not change.
r: 「なかろうと…であろうと」覆盖“不是故意”和“是故意”两种情况。
re: なかろうと…であろうと covers both “not intentional” and “intentional”.

cn: 你反不反对，我都打算一个人去。
en: Whether you object or not, I intend to go alone.
r: 「ようとしまいと」是“做或不做都……”。
re: ようとしまいと means whether you do it or not.

cn: 读不读研究生犹豫到最后，因为找到了好工作，决定就业。
en: After agonizing over graduate school, I found a good job and decided to work.
r: 「ようか…まいか」是“做还是不做”的犹豫。
re: ようか…まいか is the hesitation “shall I or not”.

cn: 下周的会来也好不来也好，请务必先看资料。
en: Whether or not you come to next week’s meeting, please read the materials.
r: 「にしろ…にしろ」是“无论是……还是……”。
re: にしろ…にしろ means “whether… or…”.

cn: 即便缺席，也请联系一声。
en: Even if you are absent, please let us know.
r: 「にせよ」是“即便……也”。
re: にせよ means “even if…”.

cn: 那东西说有趣也好、说稀奇也好，总之很特别。
en: Interesting, or odd — either way, it is unusual.
r: 「というか…というか」是“说是……还是说是……”，用来不好归类。
re: というか…というか gropes for how to describe something.

cn: 那位记者犹豫要不要刊登，最后还是不登了。
en: The reporter agonized over publishing the article and in the end did not.
r: 「ようか…まいか悩んだあげく」是犹豫之后的结果。
re: ようか…まいか plus あげく: the result after wavering.

cn: 既然已经是社会人，无论做什么都必须对自己的行为负责。
en: Now that you are an adult, you must take responsibility whatever you do.
r: 「何をするにせよ」是“无论做什么都……”。
re: 何をするにせよ means “whatever you do”.

cn: 她还年轻，可论经验和能力都无可挑剔。
en: She is still young, but both her experience and her ability are impeccable.
r: 「といい…といい」是“无论从……还是从……来看”。
re: といい…といい evaluates from both angles.

cn: 被猫抓了，脸也好手也好都没放过。
en: The cat scratched me all over, face and hands alike.
r: 「といわず…といわず」是“不论……还是……都”。
re: といわず…といわず means both places, without exception.

cn: 这么无聊的商品，卖的一方离谱，买的一方也离谱。
en: Such a worthless product — the sellers are as bad as the buyers.
r: 「ほうも…ほうなら、ほうも…ほうだ」两边一起批评。
re: The repeated ほうなら…ほうだ criticizes both sides.

cn: 他嘴里总塞着口香糖啦糖果啦什么的。
en: He always has gum or candy or something in his mouth.
r: 「だの…だの」随意列举例子。
re: だの…だの lists examples casually.

cn: A“那是田中的妈妈吧。真显眼。”B“女儿那样，妈妈也那样。”
en: A: “That’s Tanaka’s mother, isn’t she? Flashy.” B: “Like daughter, like mother.”
r: 「娘が娘なら母親も母親」是“有其女必有其母”这类成对评价。
re: AがAならBもBだ pairs the two as being alike.

cn: 姐姐嫌设计旧、嫌颜色不喜欢，可她送的包我一直在用。
en: My sister complains the design is old and she dislikes the color, but I still use the bag she gave me.
r: 「だの…だのといって」把抱怨的内容一一列举。
re: だの…だのといって lists the complaints.

cn: 他成绩也好、长相也好都不出众，所以完全不受女生欢迎。
en: Neither his grades nor his looks stand out, so girls are not interested in him at all.
r: 「といい…といい」从成绩和长相两方面说都不行。
re: といい…といい covers both grades and looks.

cn: 从早上起雪下一阵停一阵。
en: Since this morning the snow has kept starting and stopping.
r: 「ては…、ては」表示动作反复交替。
re: ては…ては repeats two alternating actions.

cn: 学生时代他和我成绩上你追我赶。
en: In our student days he and I kept overtaking each other in the rankings.
r: 「つ…つ」是两个相对动作反复：超过又被超过。
re: The つ…つ pair is two opposing actions in turn.

cn: 年轻时常常喝了酒就跳舞。
en: When I was young I would drink and then dance.
r: 「ては」这里是“一……就……”的反复习惯。
re: ては here is a repeated habit: drink, then dance.

cn: 学过的东西记住又忘掉，记住又忘掉。
en: I keep remembering what I studied and then forgetting it.
r: 「ては…ては」表示记住和忘记反复。
re: ては…ては: remembering and forgetting over and over.

cn: 虽说迟到了，可电车出了事故也没办法。
en: You were late, but there is nothing to be done about a train accident.
r: 「ては」接在「事故だ」后：既然发生了事故，就无法责备。
re: ては after 事故だ: given that accident, it cannot be helped.

cn: 这篇作文太差了。错这么多，改一点也好不了。
en: This composition is awful. With this many mistakes, fixing a few will not help.
r: 「多くては」是“既然多到这个地步，（改一点）也没用”。
re: 多くては: given how many there are, a small fix will not do.

cn: 打折会场推来挤去，挤得人喘不过气。
en: The sale was such a crush of pushing both ways that it was hard to breathe.
r: 「押しつ押されつ」是“互相推挤”的反复。
re: 押しつ押されつ is pushing and being pushed.

cn: 没有工作，每天和朋友玩。也不知道是闲还是忙。
en: I have no job and play with friends every day. Am I free, or busy?
r: 「のやら…のやら」是说不清是哪种状态。
re: のやら…のやら means you cannot tell which it is.

cn: 养宠物是麻烦，可没有宠物的生活也无法想象。
en: A pet is a lot of work, but I cannot imagine life without one.
r: 「いたらいたで」是“有是有（也有麻烦），可是……”。
re: たら…たで concedes the downside and still wants it.

cn: 公司好像要倒闭。不知会变成什么样。
en: The company seems about to fail. Who knows what will happen.
r: 「ことやら」表示结果难以预料，带担心。
re: ことやら shows an uncertain, worrying outcome.

cn: 他可以说老实，也可以说消极，总之话很少。
en: You could call him quiet or passive; either way he says little.
r: 「とも…とも言える」两边都能说得通。
re: とも…とも言える: both descriptions fit.

cn: 不愿意的话就明说。
en: If you do not want to, say so plainly.
r: 「いやならいやで」是“如果不愿意，就按不愿意来处理（请直说）”。
re: なら…で: if that is the case, act on it plainly.

cn: “披萨店的传单在哪？扔掉了也就算了。”
en: “Where is the pizza flyer? If you threw it away, that is fine.”
r: 「捨てたら捨てたでいい」是“扔了就扔了，也没关系”。
re: たら…たでいい accepts the result if it already happened.

cn: 这工作不知何时才能做完，完全看不出头绪。
en: I have no idea when this job will ever end.
r: 「ことやら」表示完成的时候无法预料。
re: ことやら: there is no telling when it ends.

cn: 不想来可以不来。只不过你会吃亏而已。
en: You need not come if you do not want to. You will only be the one who loses out.
r: 「までだ」是“大不了只是……而已”。
re: までだ means “it only comes to…”.

cn: 用不着父母出面，孩子们自己就把问题解决了。
en: The children solved it themselves; the parents did not even need to step in.
r: 「までもなく」是“用不着做到……那种程度”。
re: までもなく means there is no need to go that far.

cn: 和他虽然谈不上聊天，打招呼还是会打的。
en: I may not talk with him, but I do at least say hello.
r: 「ないまでも」是“即便做不到……，至少……”。
re: ないまでも: even if not that much, at least…

cn: 无论赚多少钱，死了也就到头了。
en: However much money you make, once you die that is the end of it.
r: 「それまでだ」是“到此为止、一切归零”。
re: それまでだ means that is the end of it.

cn: 这么点故障，用不着请人修。我来给你弄好。
en: A fault this small does not need a repairman. I will fix it.
r: 「までもない」是“犯不上、不必”。
re: までもない means it is not worth going that far.

cn: 想变好的话，只有一个办法：拼命练。
en: If you want to get good, all you can do is practice hard.
r: 「までのことだ」是“不过就是……而已／只须如此”。
re: までのことだ reduces it to one simple course.

cn: 他的行为用不着搬出法律，也可以说是犯罪吧。
en: His act can be called a crime without even bringing the law into it.
r: 「までもなく」：不必抬出法律就已经够得上犯罪。
re: までもなく: no need to invoke the law.

cn: 我支持的队输了比赛，遗憾极了。
en: The team I supported lost, and I could not be more disappointed.
r: 「限りだ」接在感情词后，表示程度到了极点。
re: 限りだ after a feeling means “extremely”.

cn: 买了新房。从这个月起就要和这套公寓告别了。
en: I bought a new house. This month is the last I will see of this apartment.
r: 「を限りに」是“以……为最后一次”。
re: を限りに means “ending with…”.

cn: 感冒的时候，与其吃药，不如好好睡一觉。
en: When you have a cold, sleeping is better than taking medicine.
r: 「に限る」是“最好莫过于……”。
re: に限る means nothing beats this.

cn: 早班电车拥挤，并不是只有今天才这样。
en: Crowded morning trains are not something that happens only today.
r: 「に限ったことではない」是“并不只限于……”。
re: に限ったことではない: it is not limited to this case.

cn: 中了彩票，真是羡慕得不得了。
en: Winning the lottery — I could not be more envious.
r: 「うらやましい限りだ」把羡慕说到极点。
re: 限りだ pushes the envy to the limit.

cn: 那部剧收视率上不去，到第十集就停播了。
en: The drama’s ratings never rose, and it was cancelled with the tenth episode.
r: 「を限りに」：以第十集为最后。
re: を限りに: the tenth episode is the last.

cn: 写不出汉字并不是最近才有的事，从开始用电脑起就一直这样。
en: Forgetting how to write kanji is not recent; it has been so ever since I started using a computer.
r: 「に限ったことではなく」否定“只是最近”。
re: に限ったことではなく denies that it is only recent.

cn: 听邻居说，昨晚那家有人去世了。
en: According to a neighbor, someone in that house died last night.
r: 「とのことだ」转述听来的消息。
re: とのことだ reports hearsay.

cn: 虽说刚进公司，招呼能不能打得像样一点。
en: You only just joined, but could you at least manage a proper greeting?
r: 「とはいえ」是“虽说……可是”。
re: とはいえ means “that said”.

cn: 即便是父母，责骂孩子也不该动粗。
en: Even parents should not use violence when scolding a child.
r: 「といえども」是“即便是……也”。
re: といえども means “even…”.

cn: 铃木打来电话，说今天感冒请假。
en: There was a call from Suzuki saying he will be off today with a cold.
r: 「との」在这里是转述电话的内容。
re: との marks the reported content of the call.

cn: 看起来那么有女人味、那么美的人，竟然是男的。
en: Someone who looks so feminine and beautiful turned out to be a man.
r: 「とは」表示出乎意料的事实：“竟然是……”。
re: とは here marks a surprising fact.

cn: 虽说当时不知道，但还是做了失礼的事，非常抱歉。
en: I did not know, but I was still rude. I am very sorry.
r: 「とはいえ」先承认不知道，道歉仍然成立。
re: とはいえ: not knowing does not cancel the apology.

cn: 为了生活，即便是休息日也得不休息地干活。
en: To make a living I have to work even on days off.
r: 「といえども」：连休息日也不例外。
re: といえども: even a day off is no exception.

cn: 那位老师无论我问什么，总是诚恳地回答。
en: Whatever I ask, that teacher always answers sincerely.
r: 「をもって」表示手段或态度：以诚意。
re: をもって marks the means: with sincerity.

cn: 我父亲退休之后，整天就知道看电视。
en: Ever since my father retired, he watches television all day.
r: 「てからというもの」强调从那以后情况就一直如此。
re: てからというもの: ever since then, and continuously.

cn: 中奖名单的公布，以寄出奖品来代替。
en: Announcement of the winners will be replaced by sending the prizes.
r: 「をもって代える」是“以……来代替”。
re: をもって代える means to substitute one thing for another.

cn: 开始一个人生活之后，就没好好吃过一顿饭。
en: Ever since I started living alone, I have not had a proper meal.
r: 「てからというもの」同样是“自那以后一直”。
re: てからというもの again: ever since living alone.

cn: 昨天的会上，以他的发言为开端，反对意见一个接一个。
en: At yesterday’s meeting his remark set off a string of objections.
r: 「を皮切りに」是“以……为开端”。
re: を皮切りに means starting with…

cn: 那位歌手走红之后，态度好像变得傲慢了。
en: Ever since that singer became popular, their attitude seems to have grown big.
r: 「てからというもの」：走红之后一直是这种态度。
re: てからというもの: ever since becoming popular.

cn: 凭借最新技术，那项开发大概也不难。
en: With the latest technology, that development should not be hard.
r: 「をもってすれば」是“若使用……的话就能”。
re: をもってすれば: if one uses that means.

cn: 那个人总是一挤上电车就想占座位。
en: He always tries to grab a seat the moment he boards the train.
r: 「が早いか」是“刚一……就立刻”。
re: が早いか means the instant…

cn: 她一进家门，就一下子冲进了厕所。
en: The moment she entered the house, she rushed to the toilet.
r: 「や」是“一……就”，比「や否や」更短。
re: や is “as soon as”.

cn: 以为终于到了富士山山顶，结果才到八合目。
en: I thought I had finally reached the summit of Mt. Fuji, but it was only the eighth station.
r: 「と思いきや」是“原以为……结果却”。
re: と思いきや: you expect one thing and get the opposite.

cn: 一接到119报警，救护车就出动了。
en: The ambulance set out the moment the 119 call came in.
r: 「が早いか」：接到通报立刻出发。
re: が早いか: departure follows the call at once.

cn: 他平时很安静，可一旦发起火来就闹得不可收拾。
en: He is usually very quiet, but once he gets angry there is no stopping him.
r: 「たら最後」是“一旦……就完了／就停不下来”。
re: たら最後: once it happens, there is no going back.

cn: 以为贺年卡最后一张写完了，结果还剩二十张。
en: I thought I had finished the last New Year card, but twenty were still left.
r: 「かと思いきや」同样是预期落空。
re: かと思いきや reverses the expectation.

cn: 他的博客一更新，反响就接连而来。
en: The moment he updates his blog, reactions pour in.
r: 「するや」是“一……就”。
re: や means as soon as he updates.

cn: 刚吃完下一道菜就端上来，没法慢慢品味。
en: The next dish arrived as soon as I ate, so I could not savor anything.
r: 「そばから」是“刚……就（紧接着）”。
re: そばから means right after, one thing after another.

cn: 今天来一是报告前几天的事，二是介绍部下。
en: I came both to report on the other day and to introduce my subordinate.
r: 「かたがた」是做一件事顺便兼做另一件。
re: かたがた does one errand and another together.

cn: 散步顺道去的美术馆非常空。
en: The museum I dropped into while out for a walk was very empty.
r: 「がてら」是“在做某事的途中顺便”。
re: がてら means while doing something else.

cn: 那位小说家写稿之余，把弹琴当爱好。
en: Alongside writing, the novelist plays the piano as a hobby.
r: 「のかたわら」是“一边做主业，一边……”。
re: のかたわら is a side activity beside the main one.

cn: 那商品刚摆上就卖得飞快。
en: The goods sold out almost as fast as they were put on the shelf.
r: 「そばから」：刚摆上就卖掉。
re: そばから: sold the moment they were displayed.

cn: 为忘年会踩点顺便去喝的那家居酒屋，并不怎么样。
en: The izakaya we drank at while scouting for the year-end party was not very good.
r: 「がてら」：踩点顺便去喝。
re: がてら: drinking while checking the place.

cn: 今天特来拜访，一并就前几天的事致歉。
en: I have come both to apologize for the other day and to pay my respects.
r: 「かたがた」把致歉和拜访合在一次。
re: かたがた combines the apology with the visit.

cn: 也没想买什么，在百货店里闲逛，碰到了朋友。
en: I was wandering the department store without meaning to buy anything, and ran into a friend.
r: 「ともなく」是“并无明确目的地／并无特定打算”。
re: ともなく means without a particular aim.

cn: 沉默就好了，却忍不住说了多余的话。
en: I should have kept quiet, but I went and said too much.
r: 「ばいいものを」是“要是……就好了（可偏偏没有）”。
re: ばいいものを regrets that the better choice was not taken.

cn: 没有健康的身体，钱再多也不能说幸福。
en: Without a healthy body, no amount of money makes you happy.
r: 「なくしては」是“如果没有……就（不能）”。
re: なくしては: if you are without it, the result fails.

cn: 这本小说没法不流泪地读完。
en: You cannot read this novel without tears.
r: 「なしに」是“不带……地”，后接不可能。
re: なしに: without tears, which turns out to be impossible.

cn: 一下电车，不知从哪儿飘来好闻的香味。
en: When I left the station, a delicious smell came from somewhere.
r: 「どこからともなく」是“不知从何处”。
re: ともなく with どこから: from no place you can name.

cn: 不知从哪儿传来的钢琴声让我静不下心学习。
en: Piano music from somewhere keeps me from concentrating.
r: 「どこからともなく」同样是来源不明。
re: どこからともなく: the source is unknown.

cn: 要是早五分钟出门就好了，磨蹭结果没赶上电车。
en: If only I had left five minutes earlier; I dawdled and missed the train.
r: 「ばよかったものを」后悔没早出门。
re: ばよかったものを regrets not leaving earlier.

cn: 他是个很好的人。可一说到结婚，就觉得有点靠不住。
en: He is a very good person. But when it comes to marriage, he seems a bit unreliable.
r: 「となると」是“一旦话题落到……上”。
re: となると shifts to the specific case of marriage.

cn: 做父母的，孩子做了坏事就该好好训。
en: A parent should scold a child properly when the child does wrong.
r: 「たる者」是“身为……的人就应该”。
re: たる者 is the duty of someone in that position.

cn: 到了那种一流餐厅，男士就需要打领带。
en: At a first-class restaurant like that, men need a tie.
r: 「ともなると」是“一旦到了那种程度就……”。
re: ともなると: once it reaches that level.

cn: 结婚根本谈不上。我连和男人说过话都没有。
en: Marriage is out of the question. I have not even spoken with a man.
r: 「すらない」是“连……都没有”，比「ない」更强调极端。
re: すらない is “not even”.

cn: 偷窃是坏事，连小孩子都知道。
en: Even a small child knows that stealing is wrong.
r: 「ですら」是“就连……也”。
re: ですら means even that person.

cn: 连年轻的我们都难受，这酷热对老人大概更难熬。
en: Even we young people suffer, so this heat must be hard on the elderly.
r: 「ですら」把“年轻人”当作尚且如此的一方。
re: ですら: even the young find it hard.

cn: 身为内科医生，却不在意营养，让人无法理解。
en: It is hard to understand a physician who does not care about nutrition.
r: 「ともあろう者」是“身为那样身份的人竟然……”。
re: ともあろう者 criticizes someone of that standing.

cn: 旅行期间一直被好吃的招待，稍微胖了一点。
en: I was treated to food the whole trip and put on a little weight.
r: 「ずくめ」是“清一色、净是”。
re: ずくめ means nothing but that thing.

cn: 第一次滑雪净是摔，弄得满身是雪。
en: On my first ski trip I did nothing but fall and got covered in snow.
r: 「まみれ」是“沾满、浑身都是”。
re: まみれ means covered in.

cn: 那家企业被发现全公司上下一起逃税。
en: It came out that the whole company was evading taxes together.
r: 「ぐるみ」是“整个集体一起”。
re: ぐるみ means the whole group together.

cn: 据说乌鸦有和人类相当的智力。
en: Crows are said to have intelligence on a par with humans.
r: 「並み」是“与……相当的程度”。
re: 並み means on the level of.

cn: 在夏天的海边玩得满身是沙。
en: I played on the summer beach and got covered in sand.
r: 「砂まみれ」是浑身沾满沙子。
re: まみれ: covered in sand.

cn: 他一身债务，最后破产了。
en: He ended up buried in debt and went bankrupt.
r: 「まみれ」这里是被债务缠满。
re: まみれ: buried in debt.

cn: 作为女演员，她的相貌属于中等。
en: As an actress her looks are about average.
r: 「並み」是普通、中等水平，不是特别出众。
re: 並み here is merely average.

cn: 我的幸福是因为有家人。希望大家都不得病、健健康康的。
en: My happiness exists because I have a family. I want everyone healthy.
r: 「あってのもの」是“正因为有……才成立”。
re: あってのもの: it exists only because of that.

cn: 父亲哪怕是星期天，只要是工作，去哪儿都去。
en: Even on Sunday, if it is work, my father will go anywhere.
r: 「とあれば」是“如果是……的话就（不惜）”。
re: とあれば: if it is for that, he will do it.

cn: 事业能成功，是因为有大家的协助，我很感谢。
en: The business succeeded thanks to everyone’s help, and I am grateful.
r: 「あってのもの」：成功是因为有协助才有的。
re: あってのもの: success exists because of the help.

cn: 因为是决赛，那场比赛的票马上就卖光了。
en: It was the final, so the tickets sold out at once.
r: 「とあって」说明原因：既然是决赛，所以票紧。
re: とあって gives the special reason.

cn: 在信息泛滥的时代，很难选出自己需要的。
en: In an age flooded with information, choosing what you need is hard.
r: 「にあって」是“处于某种状况之中”。
re: にあって sets the situation you are in.

cn: 只要是为了自己的孩子，什么苦都能忍。
en: If it is for my own child, I can bear any hardship.
r: 「とあれば」：若是为了孩子就愿意承受。
re: とあれば: if it is for that purpose.

cn: 即便处境困难也不放弃、继续努力的他，令人佩服。
en: I take my hat off to him for keeping at it even in a hard situation.
r: 「にあっても」是“即便处于……之中也”。
re: にあっても: even while in that situation.

cn: 叫“铃木”的，这个镇上有上千个。怎么找他。
en: There are a thousand Suzukis in this town. How am I supposed to find him?
r: 「からある」接在数量后，强调“多达、不下于”。
re: からある stresses “as many as”.

cn: 三百张不止的CD，没地方放了。
en: I have nowhere to put upwards of 300 CDs.
r: 「からある」同样强调数量之多。
re: からある: no fewer than 300.

cn: 祖母常说，哪怕一粒米也不许糟蹋。
en: My grandmother often said not to waste even a single grain of rice.
r: 「たりとも…な」是“哪怕一点点也不许”。
re: たりとも…な: not even the smallest amount.

cn: 在樱花树下喝酒唱歌。这是唯有日本才有的赏花光景。
en: Drinking and singing under the cherries. A blossom-viewing scene you only get in Japan.
r: 「ならでは」是“唯有……才有”。
re: ならでは means unique to.

cn: 和那个年轻人谈谈，多少有些能共鸣的地方。
en: Talking with that young person, there was at least some common ground.
r: 「なりとも」是“哪怕多少、哪怕一点点”。
re: なりとも means even a little.

cn: 新片的看点，是只有电脑图像才有的有冲击力的画面。
en: The highlight is powerful images you only get from computer graphics.
r: 「ならではの」：唯有CG才有的魄力。
re: ならではの: a force only CG can give.

cn: 那条狗无论主人去哪儿都跟着。
en: That dog follows its owner wherever they go.
r: 「なりとも」这里和「どこへ」搭配，是“无论哪里”。
re: どこへなりとも: to wherever it may be.

cn: 只要肯花金钱和时间，连我也不见得做不到。
en: If I spend money and time, even I am not incapable of it.
r: 「ないものでもない」是委婉的肯定：也不是不能。
re: ないものでもない is a soft “it is not impossible”.

cn: 有没有什么办法能把字写漂亮呢。
en: Isn’t there some way to write characters neatly?
r: 「ないものだろうか」是希望出现某种办法。
re: ないものだろうか wishes there were a way.

cn: 她生气也不是不能理解，可也不必气成那样吧。
en: I can see why she is angry, but she need not be that angry.
r: 「なくはない」是“并非没有（可以理解的地方）”。
re: なくはない: it is not that there is no reason.

cn: 她嗓门那么大，就不能想想办法吗。
en: Her voice is so loud — can’t something be done about it?
r: 「どうにかならないものだろうか」是“就不能有个办法吗”。
re: ならないものだろうか asks if nothing can be done.

cn: 他的练习量多到没法和其他选手比。
en: His amount of practice is beyond comparison with the other athletes.
r: 「比べものにならない」是“根本不能相提并论”。
re: 比べものにならない: not in the same league.

cn: 这台电脑贵，但性能好，看折扣幅度也不是不能买。
en: It is expensive but capable, so depending on the discount it is not impossible to buy.
r: 「ないものでもない」：并非完全不能买。
re: ないものでもない: buying is not out of the question.

cn: 这个品质好到没法和其他的比。
en: The quality is so good it cannot be compared with the others.
r: 「比べものにならないほど」强调好到无法比较。
re: 比べものにならないほど: incomparably good.

cn: 回去晚了。免不了要被父亲骂吧。
en: I got home late. I will not get away without a scolding from my father.
r: 「ないではすまない」是“不这样做就过不去”。
re: ないではすまない: you cannot get by without it.

cn: 那出戏精彩到不可能不打动每一个观众。
en: The play was so good it could not fail to move everyone who saw it.
r: 「ずにはおかない」是“必然会引起……”。
re: ずにはおかない: it inevitably causes that effect.

cn: 那是触法的行为。不知道也不能就这么算了。
en: That act breaks the law. Not knowing is no excuse.
r: 「ではすまない」是“不能以……了事”。
re: ではすまない: you cannot settle it with that excuse.

cn: 父亲脑梗倒下住了院，幸好不用做手术。
en: Father collapsed with a stroke and was hospitalized, but luckily he did not need surgery.
r: 「せずにすむ」是“不必做也能了结”，这里是庆幸。
re: ずにすむ means you were spared having to do it.

cn: 税是不想交，可不能不交。
en: I do not want to pay taxes, but I cannot get away with not paying.
r: 「ずにはすまない」：不交就过不了关。
re: ずにはすまない: not paying is not an option.

cn: 虽说不知道，可既然添了麻烦，不道歉是过不去的吧。
en: You may not have known, but you caused trouble, so you cannot skip the apology.
r: 「ずにはすまない」：道歉是免不了的。
re: ずにはすまない: an apology is unavoidable.

cn: 校方对危险性很高的骑摩托上学，不可能不禁止吧。
en: The school can hardly avoid banning the dangerous practice of commuting by motorbike.
r: 「せずにはおかない」是“必然会加以禁止”。
re: せずにはおかない: they are bound to ban it.

cn: 末班电车走了，想打车钱又不够。
en: The last train had gone, and I did not even have enough money to take a taxi.
r: 「ようにも」是“想做也（做不成）”。
re: ようにも: you want to, but cannot.

cn: 我尽量用简单的话讲了词义。再往下就没法解释了。
en: I explained the meaning as simply as I could. I cannot explain it any further.
r: 「しようがない」是“没有办法再做”。
re: しようがない: there is no way left to do it.

cn: 这雨一时半会儿不像会停。
en: This rain does not look like it will stop for a while.
r: 「そうもない」是“不像会……”。
re: そうもない: it does not look likely.

cn: 台风让河水漫出来，想过桥也过不去。
en: The typhoon flooded the river, and the bridge cannot be crossed even if you try.
r: 「ようにも…ない」是想做也做不到。
re: ようにも…ない: you try and still cannot.

cn: 自行车突然冲出来，想躲也躲不开，撞上了。
en: A bicycle shot out and there was no way to avoid hitting it.
r: 「ようがない」是“毫无办法避免”。
re: ようがない: no possible way.

cn: 和那个人无论怎么谈，我觉得也不像能互相理解。
en: However much we talk, I do not think we will ever understand each other.
r: 「そうにない」是“不像会”。
re: そうにない: it does not seem it will happen.

cn: 她疼成这样不正常，还是叫救护车好。
en: The way she is hurting is not normal; you should call an ambulance.
r: 「よう」这里是样子、程度：疼的样子异常。
re: よう here is the manner: how abnormally she shows pain.

cn: 最近的电视节目，广告也太多了。
en: TV shows these days — there are far too many commercials.
r: 「ときたら」带责备或不耐烦地提出话题。
re: ときたら brings up a topic with irritation.

cn: 如图表所示，本公司的业绩在增长。
en: As the graph shows, our sales results are growing.
r: 「ごとく」是书面的“如同”。
re: ごとく is the written “just as”.

cn: 那种难题，小学生之类怎么可能解得开。
en: There is no way a mere elementary-school kid could solve a problem that hard.
r: 「ごときに」轻视对方：“区区……”。
re: ごときに looks down on the person.

cn: 说到爱喝酒的父亲，每晚喝得大醉才回来，真头疼。
en: My father and drink — he comes home dead drunk every night, and it is a problem.
r: 「ときたら」同样是又无奈又抱怨地提起。
re: ときたら complains about the person.

cn: 小孩子吵架还叫警察，也太夸张了。
en: Calling the police over a children’s fight is overdoing it.
r: 「ごときに」把孩子吵架说得很轻。
re: ごときに belittles a children’s quarrel.

cn: 听说那位总统夫人爱铺张，花钱如流水。
en: The president’s wife loved show and spent money like water.
r: 「ごとく」是“如同流水一样”。
re: ごとく: like water.

cn: 她又漂亮又有钱，被人羡慕是当然的吧。
en: On top of being beautiful she is rich, so of course everyone envies her.
r: 「ときているから」是“又加上……，所以”。
re: ときているから adds a further reason.

cn: 作为父母很惭愧，直到现在才发现女儿行为不端。
en: It is shameful as a parent, but I never noticed my daughter’s delinquency until now.
r: 「にいたるまで」是“一直到……为止”。
re: にいたるまで: right up until now.

cn: 不论理由如何，开考后不准入场。
en: Whatever the reason, you may not enter after the exam has started.
r: 「いかんによらず」是“不论……如何”。
re: いかんによらず: regardless of.

cn: 看下次考试的成绩，有可能升不了级，要努力。
en: Depending on the next exam, you may not advance, so work hard.
r: 「いかんでは」是“视……而定，有可能”。
re: いかんでは: depending on it, it may happen.

cn: 这次面试的结果将决定及格还是不及格。
en: The result of this interview will decide pass or fail.
r: 「いかんで」是“由……来决定”。
re: いかんで: it is decided by that.

cn: 昨晚的酒店火灾没有发展到大惨剧，算是过去了。
en: Last night’s hotel fire ended without becoming a major disaster.
r: 「に至らず」是“没有发展到……的地步”。
re: に至らず: it did not reach that point.

cn: 高层公寓的建设因居民反对，至今仍停在计划阶段。
en: Because residents objected, the tower plan is still only a plan to this day.
r: 「に至っている」是“一直持续到现在这种状态”。
re: に至っている: the situation has continued until now.

cn: 律师说明了A公司努力未果、终于倒闭的经过。
en: The lawyer explained how company A’s efforts failed and it went bankrupt.
r: 「に至った」是“终于落到……的结果”。
re: に至った: it ended up at that result.

cn: 那位歌手的人气不只停在日本，还传到了亚洲各国。
en: The singer’s popularity did not stop at Japan; it spread across Asia.
r: 「にとどまらず」是“不限于……还”。
re: にとどまらず: not limited to, and also…

cn: 昨天又是假日又难得放晴，游乐园非常挤。
en: Yesterday a holiday and rare clear weather together made the amusement park packed.
r: 「とあいまって」是两个因素叠在一起。
re: とあいまって: two factors combine.

cn: 股价暴跌不只是那年，过了年还在继续。
en: The stock crash did not stop that year; it continued into the new year.
r: 「にとどまらず」：不限于那一年。
re: にとどまらず: not only that year.

cn: 那部电影加上主题曲走红，成了大热门。
en: The film became a huge hit, helped by the popularity of its theme song.
r: 「と相まって」是与另一因素相辅相成。
re: と相まって: together with another factor.

cn: 车站前的荞麦面店外表又旧又寒酸，味道却出了名地好。
en: The soba shop by the station looks old and shabby, but it is famous for being good.
r: 「によらず」是“并不因为外表（就不好）”。
re: によらず: not according to the shabby look.

cn: 据说消费税上调加上不景气，下滑的个人消费很难恢复。
en: The tax rise together with the recession is said to make a recovery in spending hard.
r: 「と相まって」：两个不利因素叠在一起。
re: と相まって combines the two negative factors.

cn: 不光没有奖金，连工资都要被砍，太受打击了。
en: Not only is the bonus gone, even the salary will be cut. It is a shock.
r: 「にとどまらず」：不止奖金，还波及工资。
re: にとどまらず: it does not stop at the bonus.

cn: 妻子为了回到职场，正在找一岁孩子的托儿处。
en: My wife is looking for care for our one-year-old so she can return to work.
r: 「べく」是“为了要做到……”。
re: べく means in order to.

cn: 制造杀人的工具之类，是不可允许的。
en: Making tools for killing is something that must not be allowed.
r: 「べからざる」是书面的“不该、不可”。
re: べからざる is the written “must not”.

cn: 立着一块牌子，写着“禁止进入草坪”。
en: There was a sign saying “Do not enter the lawn.”
r: 「べからず」是告示上的禁止。
re: べからず is the prohibition on signs.

cn: 战争中的经历，对谁都是不该忘记的悲惨事情。
en: The wartime experience is a tragedy no one should forget.
r: 「べからざる」是“不应被忘记的”。
re: べからざる: that must not be forgotten.

cn: 为了考上日语能力考试N1，我日夜在学。
en: I study day and night in order to pass JLPT N1.
r: 「べく」表示目的。
re: べく states the purpose.

cn: 现在明明是夏天却下雪，有的地方正发生着不该有的现象。
en: Snow in summer — some regions are seeing something that should not happen.
r: 「あるべからざる」是“不该发生的”。
re: あるべからざる: something that ought not to exist.

cn: 为了当律师而拼命坚持的努力有了结果，考试通过了。
en: The effort kept up in order to become a lawyer paid off, and the exam was passed.
r: 「べく」：以成为律师为目的而持续的努力。
re: べく: the effort aimed at becoming a lawyer.

cn: 去年夏天雨也少，可今年的缺水比去年更严重。
en: Last summer had little rain too, but this year’s water shortage is worse.
r: 「にもまして」是“比……更”。
re: にもまして means even more than.

cn: 在CD发售之前，先开了那位艺人的演唱会。
en: A concert by that artist was held ahead of the CD release.
r: 「に先駆けて」是“赶在……之前”。
re: に先駆けて means ahead of.

cn: 音乐节上那位女歌手的服装比上次更华丽了。
en: At the festival that singer’s costume was even flashier than last time.
r: 「にもまして」：比上一次更。
re: にもまして: even more than the previous time.

cn: 朋友的儿子那么优秀，反观我家孩子怎么这么不行。
en: My friend’s son is outstanding; by contrast, how poorly my own child does.
r: 「にひきかえ」是“与……相反”。
re: にひきかえ contrasts the two.

cn: 不跟上时代的想法，就不会被年轻人接受。
en: If your thinking does not fit the times, young people will not accept it.
r: 「にそくした」是“符合、贴合”。
re: にそくした means in line with.

cn: 这是赶在全国发售之前，只在本店先行发售的商品。
en: This item goes on sale here ahead of the nationwide release.
r: 「に先駆けて」：先于全国发售。
re: に先駆けて: before the national release.

cn: 哥哥很靠谱，弟弟却吊儿郎当，让人发愁。
en: The older brother is reliable; the younger one, by contrast, is careless.
r: 「にひきかえ」拿哥哥和弟弟对比。
re: にひきかえ sets the brother against the younger one.

cn: 太忙了，本想过会儿吃午饭，结果一直没吃，到了晚饭时间。
en: I was busy and meant to eat lunch later, but I never did, and it was dinner time.
r: 「ずじまい」是“最终没能做成”。
re: ずじまい means it ended without happening.

cn: 请把感想照实写在问卷上。
en: Please write your impressions on the questionnaire just as you feel them.
r: 「思うままに」是“照自己所想、不受限制”。
re: ままに means just as you think.

cn: 他虽然看不见，却演奏得很精彩，打动了观众。
en: Though he cannot see, he played wonderfully and moved the audience.
r: 「ずとも」是“即使不……也”。
re: ずとも means even without.

cn: 店员一推荐，我就照单买了台很贵的电视。
en: I bought an expensive television just as the clerk recommended.
r: 「れるままに」是“任由对方……就照做了”。
re: ままに: he went along with the recommendation.

cn: 好像把见面地点搞错了，结果一直没见着她。
en: I seem to have got the meeting place wrong, and in the end I never saw her.
r: 「ずじまい」：最终没有见成。
re: ずじまい: it ended without meeting.

cn: 本想再向医生问细一点检查结果，却被护士催着离开了诊室。
en: I meant to ask the doctor more, but left the room as the nurse urged me.
r: 「ながらも」想问却没问成，「促されるまま」是顺着催促离开。
re: ながらも is the unfulfilled wish; まま follows the urging.

cn: 今天本想早点回去，却被人一邀就来喝酒了。
en: I meant to go home early today, but I came drinking as soon as I was invited.
r: 「誘われるまま」是“被邀请了就顺着去了”。
re: まま: he went along with the invitation.

cn: 明明觉得人内在比外表重要，却还是会被好看的外表吸引。
en: I think character matters more than looks, and yet looks still catch my eye.
r: 「ながらも」是“虽然……却”。
re: ながらも: although, and yet.

cn: 这部电影故事内容自不必说，画面之美也很受好评。
en: The story is praised, and the beauty of the images is too.
r: 「もさることながら」是“……自不必说，……也”。
re: もさることながら: not only that, but also.

cn: 他虽然差点摔倒，还是滑下了陡坡。
en: He nearly fell, but still skied down the steep slope.
r: 「ながらも」：尽管快摔倒了仍然滑下去。
re: ながらも: despite nearly falling.

cn: 既然约好了，即便下雪也不得不去。
en: Having promised, I have to go even if it snows.
r: 「手前」是顾及已经说出的承诺，所以不能反悔。
re: 手前: having committed yourself, you cannot back out.

cn: 八岁的儿子还是个孩子，却拼命攒钱给我买了生日礼物，那是一生的宝贝。
en: My eight-year-old saved hard, child though he is, and the present is a treasure for life.
r: 「ながらに」是“虽然还是孩子，却……”。
re: ながらに: even while still a child.

cn: 日本队虽然打得很苦，还是勉强拿到了铜牌。
en: Japan struggled, but just managed to take the bronze.
r: 「しながらも」是“虽然苦战却仍然”。
re: ながらも: despite the hard fight.

cn: 他的演讲内容自不必说，表现力和魄力也必然打动听众。
en: Not only the content but the delivery was bound to move the listeners.
r: 「もさることながら」先肯定内容，再强调表现力。
re: もさることながら adds force of delivery on top of content.

cn: 用心做的菜，孩子们却一脸难吃地皱起了脸。
en: I cooked with care, but the children grimaced as if it tasted bad.
r: 「とばかりに」是“简直就像在说……似的”。
re: とばかりに: as if to say.

cn: 我家的狗一看见我就几乎要扑上来似的跑过来。
en: Our dog runs at me as if it is about to jump up the moment it sees me.
r: 「んばかり」是“几乎要……的样子”。
re: んばかり: on the verge of.

cn: 她一副累坏了的样子，进门就倒在床上。
en: As if to say she was exhausted, she fell onto the bed the moment she entered.
r: 「とばかりに」把疲惫表现得像一句话。
re: とばかりに acts out the feeling of exhaustion.

cn: 他为了把技术练到极致，夜里也不睡地努力。
en: He works through the night in order to perfect his skill.
r: 「んがために」是书面的“为了要……”。
re: んがために is the written “in order to”.

cn: 正因为人们对那种病缺乏了解，他们才受到迫害。
en: They were persecuted precisely because people knew so little about the disease.
r: 「ゆえに」是“因为”，偏书面。
re: ゆえに is a written “because”.

cn: 接触到那个国家满是笑容的孩子们，我的人生观变了。
en: Meeting children there who were all smiles changed how I see life.
r: 「んばかりの」形容笑容多到快要溢出来。
re: んばかりの: smiles on the point of overflowing.

cn: 他犯了重罪，但事发时还是判断力不成熟的未成年人，所以得以回归社会。
en: He committed a serious crime, but because he was still a minor he could return to society.
r: 「がゆえ」说明“正因为是未成年人”这一原因。
re: がゆえ gives the reason: precisely because he was a minor.

cn: 除了这份工作，大概没有更适合他的了。
en: Aside from this job, there is probably no work that suits him better.
r: 「をおいて」是“除了……之外（没有）”。
re: をおいて means aside from, there is no other.

cn: 她对自己的失败置若罔闻，净批评别人。
en: She ignores her own failures and only criticizes others.
r: 「をよそに」是“把……丢在一边、不管”。
re: をよそに means ignoring that.

cn: 兼着观光，去澳大利亚进修了。
en: I went to Australia for training and sightseeing at the same time.
r: 「をかねて」是“兼做”。
re: をかねて combines two purposes.

cn: 不顾附近居民反对，高层公寓还是盖起来了。
en: The tower was built in spite of the neighbors’ opposition.
r: 「をよそに」：把反对丢在一边。
re: をよそに ignores the opposition.

cn: 她经过结婚、生子，又回到了赛场。
en: She returned to competition after marriage and childbirth.
r: 「を経て」是“经过……之后”。
re: を経て means after going through.

cn: 那家企业不管不景气造成其他公司业绩低迷，自己的销售额却在增长。
en: While other firms slump in the recession, that company is growing sales anyway.
r: 「をよそに」：对别家的低迷毫不在意。
re: をよそに: paying no mind to the others’ slump.

cn: 今年的贺年卡因为兼着报告搬家，比往年多。
en: This year’s cards also reported the move, so there were more than usual.
r: 「も兼ねていたゆえに」：正因为兼了搬家报告，数量才多。
re: 兼ねる plus ゆえに: because they also served as the moving notice.

cn: 以那场大地震为契机，各地都在重新审视抗震对策。
en: That earthquake prompted a review of earthquake measures everywhere.
r: 「を機に」是“以……为契机”。
re: を機に marks the turning point.

cn: 您到附近来的时候，请一定顺道来坐坐。
en: If you are ever nearby, please do drop in.
r: 「の折には」是“在……的时候”，用于邀请。
re: の折には is “on the occasion of”.

cn: 我想在迄今的意见之上，决定是否采用这个方案。
en: Taking the opinions so far into account, I want to decide whether to adopt this plan.
r: 「を踏まえて」是“在……的基础上”。
re: を踏まえて means based on.

cn: 她以结婚为前提辞去了工作。
en: She left her job on the premise of getting married.
r: 「を前提として」是“以……为前提”。
re: を前提として sets the assumption.

cn: 据说人一过四十岁，衰老就会突然加快。
en: People say aging speeds up once you pass forty.
r: 「を境に」是“以……为界”。
re: を境に marks the dividing line.

cn: 孩子出生之后，他改掉了以往的生活态度，开始认真工作。
en: After the child was born he changed his ways and started working seriously.
r: 「を境に」：以孩子出生为界，前后不同。
re: を境に: the birth is the dividing line.

cn: 这辆自行车是以身高160厘米以上的人为使用前提制造的。
en: This bicycle is made on the assumption that the rider is at least 160 cm tall.
r: 「を前提として」说明设计时假定的使用者。
re: を前提として states the assumed user.

cn: 家里闷着一股怪味，就把所有的窗都打开了。
en: A strange smell filled the house, so I opened every single window.
r: 「という」重复同一名词，表示“所有的、无一例外”。
re: という repeats the noun: every single one.

cn: 练一两次吉他是弹不会的。
en: You will not learn guitar with just one or two practices.
r: 「や」连接小数量：仅仅一两次。
re: や links small numbers: merely one or two.

cn: 他努力了又努力，终于当上了梦寐以求的律师。
en: He piled effort on effort and finally became the lawyer he had hoped to be.
r: 「に…を重ねて」是同一行为反复累积。
re: に…を重ねる piles the same effort up.

cn: 女儿好像饿了，一个劲地吃。
en: My daughter must have been hungry; she ate and ate.
r: 「に…」重复动词，表示拼命地做。
re: The repeated verb means doing it intensely.

cn: 我的早餐总是咖啡加面包。
en: My breakfast is always coffee and bread.
r: 「に」这里是搭配：咖啡配面包。
re: に pairs the two foods.

cn: 他练习了又练习，终于成了钢琴家。
en: He practiced and practiced and finally became a pianist.
r: 「に…を重ねて」：练习不断累积。
re: に…を重ねる: practice piled on practice.

cn: 她不顾校规，把每根指甲都涂得通红。
en: Ignoring the school rules, she painted every one of her nails bright red.
r: 「をよそに」是不管校规；「爪という爪」是每一根指甲。
re: をよそに ignores the rules; という means every nail.

cn: 还在讨论中，所以没法给您明确答复。
en: It is still under discussion, so I cannot give you a clear answer.
r: 「のこととて」是“因为是……（请见谅）”。
re: のこととて explains and asks for understanding.

cn: 那么大的公司倒闭，谁也没想到。
en: Nobody even imagined a company that large would fail.
r: 「だに」是“连……都（没有）”，强调程度。
re: だに means not even.

cn: 这么便宜，只有现金交易才做得到。
en: A sale this cheap is possible only as a cash deal.
r: 「にして初めて」是“唯有采取这种方式才第一次可能”。
re: にして初めて: only when it is done this way.

cn: 他上课迟到了，连句对不起都没说就坐下了。
en: He was late to class and sat down without even apologizing.
r: 「もしない」是“连……都不做”。
re: もしない: not even that.

cn: 和外国人结婚，连做梦都没想过。
en: Marrying a foreigner was not even a dream I had.
r: 「だに…ない」是“连……都没有”。
re: だに…ない: not even in a dream.

cn: 那位女演员对跟她打招呼的粉丝看都不看就走了。
en: The actress walked off without even a glance at the fan who spoke to her.
r: 「もしない」：连看都不看。
re: もしない: not even a look.

cn: 她还是初学，多少有点失误请多包涵。
en: She is still a beginner, so please overlook a few mistakes.
r: 「のこととて」因为是初学者，请求宽容。
re: のこととて asks for leniency because she is a beginner.

cn: 他一上中学，说话就变得老成了。
en: The moment he became a junior-high student, he started sounding grown-up.
r: 「びた」是“带有……的样子”。
re: びる means to take on that quality.

cn: 装年轻穿得那么少，所以才感冒。
en: You dress too lightly trying to look young, and that is why you catch cold.
r: 「ぶって」是“故意装出……的样子”。
re: ぶる means to pose as.

cn: 对装出热心来接近你的人要小心。
en: Be careful of people who approach you pretending to be kind.
r: 「ぶって」：装作亲切。
re: ぶって: putting on a show of kindness.

cn: 作案现场写着带点谜样的字。
en: Mysterious-looking words were written at the crime scene.
r: 「めいた」是“带有……气息的”。
re: めく means having a touch of.

cn: 电视介绍了选手活跃的样子。
en: The players’ fine performances were shown on television.
r: 「ぶり」是某种样子、状态。
re: ぶり is the manner of doing.

cn: 他装成熟客在讲那家店，其实好像一次都没去过。
en: He talked about the shop like a regular, but it seems he had never been.
r: 「ぶって」是装出常客的样子。
re: ぶって: posing as a regular.

cn: 出版社收到大量像是反驳那篇报道的邮件。
en: The publisher got a flood of mail that sounded like rebuttals of the article.
r: 「めいた」是“带有反驳意味的”。
re: めいた: something with the air of a rebuttal.

cn: 电车里有个醉汉大声说着不堪入耳的话。
en: On the train a drunk was shouting words too awful to listen to.
r: 「にたえない」是“不忍、不堪”。
re: にたえない: unbearable to listen to.

cn: 学生生活的美好回忆，是遇到了值得信赖的老师。
en: The good memory of student life is meeting a teacher worth trusting.
r: 「にたる」是“值得……”。
re: にたる means worthy of.

cn: 这件衬衫是用经得起每天洗的面料做的。
en: This shirt is made of fabric that stands up to daily washing.
r: 「にたえる」是“经得起、耐受”。
re: にたえる means it can withstand.

cn: 交通事故现场的照片，尽是不忍卒看的画面。
en: The accident photos are all too awful to look at.
r: 「にたえない」：看不下去。
re: にたえない: too much to look at.

cn: 这本书内容好，值得推荐给孩子们。
en: This book is good enough to recommend to children.
r: 「に足る」是“足以、值得”。
re: に足る means sufficient, worth doing.

cn: 没有值得相信的信息，就说不出明确的话。
en: Without information worth believing, nothing definite can be said.
r: 「に足る」：值得信赖的信息。
re: に足る: information that is worth trusting.

cn: 她的演技接连失败，实在不忍卒看。
en: Her acting was one failure after another, too painful to watch.
r: 「にたえない」：看不下去。
re: にたえない: unbearable to watch.

cn: 最近的年轻女孩把指甲涂成黑的绿的，难看死了。
en: Girls these days paint their nails black or green — it is unbearably ugly.
r: 「といったらありゃしない」把不好的程度说到极点。
re: といったらありゃしない pushes a bad quality to the limit.

cn: 昨天晚会上他的态度无礼到了极点。
en: His manner at yesterday’s party was as rude as could be.
r: 「といったらなかった」同样是程度极端。
re: といったらなかった: extremely rude.

cn: 自己的孩子会犯下这种罪，可悲到了极点。
en: That my own child would commit such a crime is as pathetic as it gets.
r: 「といったらない」把“可悲”说到极点。
re: といったらない: nothing is more pathetic.

cn: 无论被邀请多少次，那种地方我才不去。
en: No matter how often I am invited, I am not going to a place like that.
r: 「やしない」是强烈的否定：“才不会”。
re: やしない is an emphatic “I will not”.

cn: 到夏天我要瘦下十公斤给你看。
en: I will show you — I will lose ten kilos by summer.
r: 「てみせる」是下决心做给别人看。
re: てみせる is a determined “I’ll show you”.

cn: 他知道后似乎受了很大打击，慌张的样子简直没法说。
en: The news hit him hard; you should have seen how flustered he was.
r: 「といったらなかった」形容慌张到了极点。
re: といったらなかった: his panic was extreme.

cn: 前几天的比赛比分拉开了，输了也谈不上可惜。
en: The score was so wide that losing was not even regrettable.
r: 「もなんともない」是“一点也不（可惜）”。
re: もなんともない: not … in the least.

cn: 面试结果会电话联系，不必特意过来。
en: We will phone the interview result, so you need not come here.
r: 「には及びません」是“不必、用不着”。
re: には及びません means there is no need.

cn: 这次交通事故，不得不说是行人一方不注意。
en: As for this accident, one has to say it was the pedestrian’s carelessness.
r: 「ざるをえない」是“不得不”。
re: ざるをえない: cannot help but.

cn: 那部电影里，主人公和看不见的敌人战斗的样子令人印象深刻。
en: In that film, the hero fighting an unseen enemy stays with you.
r: 「ざる」是古语否定：看不见的敌人。
re: ざる is the old negative: an enemy that is not seen.

cn: 比不上京都，这个镇上寺庙也很多。
en: It does not match Kyoto, but this town has many temples too.
r: 「にはおよばない」是“及不上、比不上”。
re: にはおよばない: it does not come up to.

cn: 他说的没错，所以大概不得不接受。
en: What he says is not wrong, so you will probably have to accept it.
r: 「ざるを得ない」是“不得不”。
re: ざるを得ない: you have no choice but to accept.

cn: 达·芬奇在绘画和雕塑上自不必说，在哲学思想和自然科学上也给后世留下很多影响。
en: Da Vinci left a mark not only in painting and sculpture but also in philosophy and science.
r: 「は言うにおよばず」是“……自不必说，连……也”。
re: 言うにおよばず: needless to say, and also.

cn: 虽然违背自己的意愿，已经决定的事我也不得不接受。
en: It went against my wishes, but I had to accept what had been decided.
r: 「ざるを得なかった」是过去的“不得不”。
re: ざるを得なかった: there was no choice.

cn: 幼儿园时的朋友，别说名字，连脸都忘了。
en: I have forgotten not only the names of my kindergarten friends but even their faces.
r: 「はおろか」是“别说……连……也”。
re: はおろか: not just A, but even B.

cn: 从前也许还说得通，现在没人会信那种迷信了吧。
en: It might have been different long ago, but nobody believes that superstition now.
r: 「ならいざしらず」是“以前的事另当别论”。
re: ならいざしらず sets the past aside.

cn: 工作的事先放一放，今天尽情玩吧。
en: Never mind work talk — let’s enjoy ourselves today.
r: 「はさておき」是“暂且不提”。
re: はさておき sets a topic aside.

cn: 听说附近进了小偷，别说现金，连冰箱里的东西都被偷了。
en: A thief got in nearby; not only the cash but even the food in the fridge was taken.
r: 「はおろか」：现金自不必说，连冰箱里的也没了。
re: はおろか: cash, and even the fridge.

cn: 无论什么理由，入会费都不予退还。
en: Whatever the reason, the membership fee will not be refunded.
r: 「であれ」是“无论是什么样的……”。
re: であれ: whatever the reason.

cn: 最近有的大学生别说论文，连报告怎么写都不知道。
en: Some students these days do not even know how to write a short report, let alone a thesis.
r: 「はおろか…すら」一层比一层更基本的事都不会。
re: はおろか…すら: not even the more basic skill.

cn: 难的问题先放一边，从看上去马上能解决的开始动手吧。
en: Set the hard problems aside and start with the ones that look solvable.
r: 「はさておき」：难题暂且不谈。
re: はさておき leaves the hard ones for later.

cn: 从状况判断，不难想象他就是犯人。
en: Judging from the situation, it is not hard to imagine that he is the culprit.
r: 「にかたくない」是“不难……”。
re: にかたくない: it is not hard to.

cn: 即便科长辞职了，也没什么好惊讶的。
en: Even if the section chief quits, it is not something to be surprised at.
r: 「にはあたらない」是“犯不上、不必”。
re: にはあたらない: there is no call for it.

cn: 他在法庭上主张无罪，可他做的事不是杀人又是什么。
en: He claims innocence in court, but what he did is nothing if not murder.
r: 「でなくてなんだろう」是反问：不是这个又是什么。
re: でなくてなんだろう: what else could it be.

cn: 母亲去世十多年了，父亲仍然深深爱着她。
en: More than ten years after Mother died, Father still loves her deeply.
r: 「てやまない」是“一直……不已”。
re: てやまない: the feeling does not stop.

cn: 不难体察失去双亲的她的心情。
en: It is not hard to imagine how she feels after losing both parents.
r: 「にかたくない」：不难体察。
re: にかたくない: not hard to sense.

cn: 只晚了五分钟左右，犯不上生气吧。
en: Being about five minutes late is hardly something to get angry about.
r: 「にはあたらない」：不必为这点事生气。
re: にはあたらない: no need to be angry.

cn: 为了孩子甚至工作到生病，这不是父母的爱又是什么。
en: Working until you fall ill for your child — what is that if not a parent’s love?
r: 「でなくてなんだろう」用反问肯定这就是爱。
re: でなくてなんだろう affirms that this is love.

cn: 即便说不在乎输赢，还是赢了更好。
en: Even if you say you do not care who wins, winning is still better.
r: 「に越したことはない」是“再好不过、越……越好”。
re: に越したことはない: nothing is better than.

cn: 欲望说起来没完，就决定买这套公寓吧。
en: If you start on what you want there is no end, so let’s take this apartment.
r: 「ときりがない」是“一……就没完”。
re: ときりがない: once you start, there is no end.

cn: 性能一样的话，价格便宜再好不过。
en: If the performance is the same, cheaper is always better.
r: 「に越したことはない」：越便宜越好。
re: に越したことはない: the cheaper the better.

cn: 这个地方吸烟也没有关系。
en: There is no problem with smoking in this place.
r: 「差し支えない」是“不妨、没有妨碍”。
re: 差し支えない means it is all right.

cn: 抱怨起来没完，可也不能辞掉现在的公司。
en: I could complain forever, but I cannot quit this company.
r: 「ときりがない」：不满一说就没尽头。
re: ときりがない: the complaints never end.

cn: 有资格对找工作有利。能拿的话还是拿了好，能考就考吧。
en: A qualification helps you get a job. Better to have it if you can, so take it if you can.
r: 「に越したことはない」：有总比没有好。
re: に越したことはない: better to have it.

cn: 说没有经验也没关系，我就去应聘了，结果其他应聘者全是有经验的。
en: They said no experience was fine, so I applied — and everyone else had experience.
r: 「差し支えない」：没有经验也不碍事。
re: 差し支えない: lack of experience is acceptable.

cn: 每看到政治家贪污，就禁不住愤怒。
en: Whenever I see politicians’ corruption, I cannot hold back my anger.
r: 「につけ」是“每当……就”；「禁じ得ない」是“禁不住”。
re: につけ is “whenever”; 禁じ得ない cannot be suppressed.

cn: 昨天他们的演唱会上，甚至有女孩激动得昏了过去。
en: At their concert yesterday, things got so heated that a girl fainted.
r: 「しまつだ」是把事情说成落到了糟糕的地步。
re: しまつだ: it came to that extreme.

cn: 她有把话说得很夸张的倾向，你听的时候留心一点。
en: She tends to exaggerate, so listen with that in mind.
r: 「きらいがある」是“有……的倾向”，多指不太好的倾向。
re: きらいがある is a tendency, often an undesirable one.

cn: 说是很快能好的伤，因为硬撑，结果不得不做手术。
en: They said the injury would heal quickly, but forcing it meant surgery.
r: 「を余儀なくされた」是“被迫不得不”。
re: を余儀なくされる: forced into it.

cn: 我家女儿节食过度病了，落到住院的地步。
en: Our daughter dieted so hard she got sick and ended up in hospital.
r: 「始末だ」是结果糟到这种地步。
re: 始末だ: it ended up this badly.

cn: 田中被指出过于慎重，有缺乏积极性的倾向。
en: Tanaka was told he is too cautious and tends to lack initiative.
r: 「きらいがある」：有这种（消极的）倾向。
re: きらいがある names the tendency.

cn: 他迟到了却还说想早退，让人怀疑他到底有没有干劲。
en: He arrived late and then asked to leave early. You wonder if he is motivated at all.
r: 「始末で」把这种行为说成落到了不像话的地步。
re: 始末で: behavior that has come to this.

cn: 我在穷到极点的环境里长大，从来没有在外面吃过饭。
en: I grew up in the poorest of circumstances and never ate out.
r: 「極まりない」是“……到了极点”。
re: 極まりない: extremely.

cn: 战争持续的那个地区，人们的生活悲惨到了极点。
en: Life for people in that long war zone is miserable in the extreme.
r: 「極まりない」把悲惨说到极点。
re: 極まりない: as miserable as can be.

cn: 那部电影极其残酷的场面被剪掉了。
en: The film’s extremely cruel scene was cut.
r: 「極まる」是“极其”。
re: 極まる means utterly.

cn: 能见到您这样的大明星，感激之至。
en: Meeting a great star like you is an honor beyond words.
r: 「の至り」是“……之至”。
re: の至り: the height of that feeling.

cn: 对您也许是日常，对我却是奢侈到了极点。
en: It may be ordinary for you, but for me it is the height of luxury.
r: 「の極み」是“……的极致”。
re: の極み: the ultimate degree.

cn: 在加油站抽烟，是危险到极点的行为。
en: Smoking at a gas station is an extremely dangerous thing to do.
r: 「極まりない」：危险之至。
re: 極まりない: dangerous in the extreme.

cn: 我的研究得到那样的评价，真是感激之至。
en: That my research was rated so highly is a deep honor.
r: 「の至り」：感激到了极点。
re: の至り: the height of gratitude.

cn: 昨天的新闻节目里，一个接一个播出这世上不该有的景象。
en: Yesterday’s news showed scene after scene that should not exist in this world.
r: 「にあるまじき」是“身为……不该有的”。
re: にあるまじき: unbecoming, that should not be.

cn: 我知道蔬菜对身体好，可我又不是马，吃不了这么多。
en: I know vegetables are good for you, but I am not a horse — I cannot eat this many.
r: 「じゃあるまいし」是“又不是……（所以不该这样）”。
re: じゃあるまいし: it is not as if you were…

cn: 她不顾脚痛，把马拉松跑完了。
en: She ran the marathon through, making nothing of the pain in her feet.
r: 「をものともせず」是“不把……当回事、不顾”。
re: をものともせず means in spite of.

cn: 欺骗弱者骗钱，是人不应有的行为。
en: Tricking the weak out of money is something a human being should not do.
r: 「にあるまじき」：作为人不该有。
re: にあるまじき: unbecoming of a person.

cn: 人多少都会有烦恼。
en: Everyone has worries, more or less.
r: 「多かれ少なかれ」是“或多或少”。
re: 多かれ少なかれ: more or less.

cn: 吃了那个又不会死，吐出来也太夸张了。
en: It is not as if eating that would kill you. Spitting it out is overdoing it.
r: 「わけじゃあるまいし」是“又不是会……”。
re: じゃあるまいし: it is not as if.

cn: 孩子无论好事坏事，都是看着大人学着长大的。
en: For better or worse, children grow by copying adults.
r: 「につけ…につけ」是“无论是……还是……”。
re: につけ…につけ: whether good or bad.
